text: The overview names the page grid class `.plx-layout-grid` (12 columns at most, contained at 1200px), but the Anatomy lists `.plx-page-grid` (up to 16 columns) and gives different breakpoints (600, 1024, 1440px instead of 600 and 840px). Are these two different grids that both belong on this page, or is one of them outdated?
The contained grid stops at 1200px here, but the One-column layout and Panel pages say the contained layout is 960px wide. Are these two different "contained" widths on purpose?

This page says Columns collapse to one column on narrow windows, but the Two-column layout page says its columns "stay side by side at every width" and "do not stack", while the Collapse page describes collapseBelow. Which is right for Columns today?

The overview says a click on the handle opens a menu (Move earlier, Move later, Move to the start, Move to the end), but the Behavior and Anatomy sections describe only dragging and arrow keys. Does the handle menu exist, and should Behavior mention it?

The page purpose describes the whole dashboard page (several applications in one workspace), while the written Purpose describes only the widget grid (arranging widgets). Which purpose should this page carry?
"Every widget: the grid becomes one column, use fewer columns" is hard to follow. Does it mean: do not make every widget wide; if all widgets need to be wide, choose fewer columns instead?
The Panel page overview describes PageContent and Center (the page content container), not Panel. Should Panel get its own overview, and does the PageContent text belong on another page?
The Panel purpose also contains the Stack purpose and the Grid purpose, copied from those pages. Should those two sentences be removed from Panel?
"The toggle has no focus style of its own in card.css; it relies on the browser's default ring." Is this still true, or does the collapse toggle now use the Plenix focus ring like other buttons?

The Two-column layout overview describes the two-pane list-and-detail workspace (SecondaryPane), and its purpose describes the application shell, while the written Purpose describes Columns (two or three equal groups side by side). Which text belongs on this page?
"Lists whose items are read one at a time (notes, messages)" describes a list-and-detail screen (Split pane), not equal columns. Should it move to the Split pane page?
The Spacer page shows the Stack purpose and the full Stack write-up (anatomy, behavior, accessibility). Should Spacer show only its own text (push and Toolbar.Spacer) and point to Stack for the rest?
The Inset page shows the Stack purpose and the full Stack write-up. Should Inset show only its own text (inset tokens and Bleed) and point to Stack for the rest?

The "Full-screen experience" variant has placeholder text ("composed from existing Platform controls", use for "The matching page purpose", avoid "Unrelated workflows"). What should this variant say, or should it be removed?

The overview says the region "shows a shadow only while it is stuck", but there is also an "Always" variant where the shadow shows at all times. Should the overview say "by default" (only while stuck, or always with the Always option)?

The overview and the "Square (default)" variant say a swatch is square with 2px corners by default, but the anatomy says "round (default) or square". Which shape is the default? Both strings are left unchanged until you decide.

The overview says the add-a-tag field is "a text field like every other (owner, batch 268)", but the anatomy calls it a borderless text field and the focus row says it shows an underline focus shadow (fields elsewhere change only their border on focus). Is the anatomy and focus text out of date? Left unchanged.

The width rule ends "White, outlined, the height of the buttons beside it", but the contrast row says it uses the neutral fill (fill-neutral) on page surfaces. Is the field white or the neutral fill? The long width rule was not rewritten until this is settled.

The pages give different option counts for when to switch controls: Radio group says more than about seven options means a select; the Radio page says two to five options; Select says up to about ten; Combobox says fewer than seven means a select; Segmented control says two to five. Which numbers should every page use? Left unchanged.

This page says "Marking optional fields instead" is something to avoid, but the Text field, Text area and Native select "Required" variants say to mark the optional fields instead when most fields are required. Which rule is right? Left unchanged.

The Form page (and Label, Help text, Required indicator, Validation message) shows the Field page's purpose and write-up word for word. For Form in particular the purpose describes one field, not a whole form. Should Form get its own purpose (and these pages their own write-ups), or is showing Field's text intended? Left unchanged. The Field rewrites above were also applied to these copies so they stay identical.

The URL, Telephone and Password field pages show the Text field write-up, whose error example is "Enter a valid email address". Should these pages get an example that fits them, or is the shared Text field text intended? Left unchanged.

As a button the drop zone is reached with Tab, but the focus row says it has no focus style of its own. Is a focus ring missing in the component, or does the text need to say where the focus shows? Left unchanged.

The purpose of the toggle button group also describes its look (bordered joined segments, the blue tint of the chosen one, your note "look A, owner, 2026-10-14", no gray track or white thumb). Most of that look is already in the Anatomy list. Should the look leave the purpose (keeping your note with it, for example in Anatomy or Details), so the purpose only says what the component is for?

The data palette lists brown among its colors (blue, green, purple, red, brown, gray). Since the color consolidation retired Brown as a category color, is brown still one of the data colors, or should this list change?

These rows say hover, focus and invalid change "the border or the line". "The line" refers to an underlined field style, but only two looks exist now (outline and filled, both with a border). Should "or the line" be removed from these three rows?

"The field’s text and border contrast; the buttons are Buttons." is unclear: it does not say what the text and border meet (for example 4.5:1 for the text, 3:1 for the border, as other fields say). It is shared by the number input, stepper, currency, percentage and quantity pages. Which contrast figures should it state?

The searchable select picks one value, but its page shows the shared Combobox purpose ("choose one or several values ... and optionally create a value"), and the shared anatomy lists Tags and the Create option. Is that fine for this page, or should the searchable select page get its own one-value purpose?

The date range picker shows the date picker’s purpose (“Takes a date as people prefer to give it…”), which speaks of one date. Should it get its own purpose about choosing a period (a start and an end), or is the shared purpose fine?
The date-time picker shows the date picker’s purpose, which speaks only of a date. Should it get its own purpose about choosing a moment (a date and a time), or is the shared purpose fine?

The overview says it attaches “local files”, but When to use says it is for files that come from more than one source. Which is right: device files only, or several sources (for example the device and the Files app)?

Both variant pages (Inline and Chips) list “Keep selection reversible and restore explicit.” under When not to use. It is a rule, not a case to avoid, and the wording is unclear. What should Inline and Chips each say not to use them for?

Both variant pages say only “Use this composition when it fits the task.” under When to use, and both have the same description. What is the difference between Inline and Chips, and when should people pick each?

The Mouse row repeats the variant description (“Validate types, per-file size and count…”), which is about checking files, not the mouse. What should the Mouse row say (for example drop files, press Choose, press Remove)?

The parts list gives only names (Device FileInput, Selected FileRows or removable chips, Validation Notice) with no description or required/optional mark, unlike other pages. Should these be filled in? That needs facts about the component that the page does not give.

The purpose is word for word the overview (“Attach validated local files with a reversible selection.”). Should the purpose say why people use it (the need it serves) instead of repeating the overview?

This page mixes two things: the mega menu (a top navigation item with a big panel of links) and the side navigation list (NavList rows with counts, pins and folding groups). The purpose, the first two usage points and every written section describe the side list, not the mega menu. Should the side-list text move to its own page (or to Side navigation), leaving this page about the mega menu only?

Section navigation shows the navigation pane's purpose and write-up (title row, splitter, rail and so on) instead of text about sections, subpages, in-page links and tables of contents. Should it get its own purpose, or is showing the pane's write-up intended?

Saved searches shows the Search workspace's purpose and write-up (the whole advanced search page). Should it get its own purpose about keeping a named query and its filters, or is showing the search page's write-up intended?

The written purpose says the pane is "shown as an overlay on small screens", but the rest of the page (and Bottom navigation) says that on a phone it is a bottom bar plus a full screen, never a drawer. Should this purpose be changed to match (the overview purpose already does)? The same text appears on Section navigation.
Side navigation says focus is not moved into the overlay, but Bottom navigation says opening the overlay or the screen moves focus into the pane and returns it on close. Which one is right?

Product navigation says the pane's rows move with the arrow keys and the pane folds with the standard motion. The Navigation menu page says the list adds no arrow keys, and Side navigation says the pane has no motion of its own. Which is right?

This says the header links leave the bar "below the Narrow class", but the overview says the bar is the Narrow class itself, and Application header says the links leave below 840px (Medium and Narrow). Should it read "below 840px (Medium and Narrow)"?

Usage says peer views always use the contained tabs, yet the Contained variant says a page whose whole body switches should use Folder tabs, and Segmented tabs have their own uses. Should the usage line say "contained by default" instead of "always"?
The compact stepper is described as for sequences "without names", but it shows "Step 2 of 5 and the step's name". Does compact show the step's name or not?

Filter bar says a search page shows the set filters as chips under the toolbar, while the Filter panel and Quick filters pages say never to put filter chips under the command bar. Are chips allowed only on the search page, and should the other pages say so?

The page says operators should be in words, never symbols people must learn, but its read-back example uses a symbol: “Size (MB) > 40”. Should the example read “Size (MB) is more than 40”, or is the symbol meant to stay in the text view?

This line uses “Rule 2” both as the name of a rule and as an example control label (“Rule 2, Operator”). Is each control meant to be labeled with its rule number plus its role (for example “Rule 2 operator”)? I left it unchanged until you say.

“The text wraps under the thumbnail’s column” can be read two ways: the text moves below the thumbnail on a narrow width, or it stays in its own column next to the thumbnail. Which one is meant? I left it unchanged.
“The heading and count follow SectionHeading and the muted text” — does this mean the heading follows SectionHeading and the count uses muted text? I left it unchanged until you confirm.

The overview names seven text roles (body, secondary, caption, data, label, strong, title), but the component offers thirteen (also heading, eyebrow, accent, success, danger and link). Should the overview list all thirteen?
The Data style is described here as 11px, but elsewhere on the page data text is "at the secondary size" (and Secondary is 12px). Which size is right for data text on its own?
This says values in a property list use the label font with equal-width digits, not the data font. The Property list page says technical values there use the data font (Reddit Mono). Which is right?

This write-up (purpose, parts, behavior, accessibility, content) appears word for word on seven pages: Body text, Paragraph, Label, Caption, Helper text, Secondary text and Truncated text. I left it unchanged so the copies stay identical. Should it be rewritten once and shown on all of them?
Two usage points give different heading sizes: one says levels 2–4 are 18, 15 and 13px, the other says level 2 is 13px, level 3 11px, level 4 10px. Which sizes are right?
The purpose describes only the small uppercase section label (SectionHeading), but the page also covers page and section headings (levels 1–4). Should the purpose cover both?
The overview says the code sits "on the inverse surface", but the parts list says it sits on the default surface (--plx-sys-surface-default). Which is right?
The usage list names six sizes (xs to 2xl), but the behavior section also lists a 2xs size of 20px, and the Small avatar page points to "the 20px size". Should usage list 2xs too?
The Avatar write-up also appears word for word on the User identity page, so I left it unchanged to keep the copies the same. Rewrite it once for both?
Usage says a technical value sits "on the value’s baseline", but the parts list says "on the label’s baseline". Which is right?

This says "a name/value table is a DataGrid, not a PropertyList". Under the table rule you set (DataGrid for dynamic tables, Table for static ones), a static name/value table would be a Table. Should this say Table?
The Property list write-up appears word for word on four pages (Property list, Key-value pair, Attribute list, Description list), so I left it unchanged. Rewrite it once for all four?
The behavior section says a broken picture is not replaced by the icon, but the Icon thumbnail page says the icon shows when there is no picture "or it fails to load". Which is right?

The Skip link page shows the purpose and full write-up of the application frame (AppShell: header, navigation pane, main region, inspector, footer), not of the skip link. Should it get its own purpose ("lets keyboard users jump past the header and navigation to the main content")?
The Paragraph page uses a "lead" text style for the opening paragraph, but the Text component’s list of styles does not include "lead". Does the lead style exist, or should these mentions change?
This page says a caption should not be longer than two lines; the Caption style on the Body text page says not longer than one line. Which limit is right?

This page describes clamping to 2, 3 or 4 lines (lines) and a Show more option (expandable), but the Text parts list only shows one-line truncation. Do lines and expandable exist on Text, or belong to another component?

Online status shows availability in words, but its purpose and write-up are those of the presence dot on an avatar. Should it get its own purpose (for example, "shows a person’s availability in words where an avatar dot is too small or missing")?
The Presence write-up also appears word for word on the Online status page, so I left it unchanged. Rewrite it once for both?

The page says a swatch can be a button that picks a color (with a ring on the chosen one), but “When not to use” says to use the swatch picker (ColorPicker) for picking from a set. Is the button form only meant for use inside ColorPicker, or can pages use picking swatches on their own? The wording should say which.

“Only relative times and date labels (and tooltip) are Tab stops” is unclear. Does it mean any timestamp that has the tooltip turned on (which is on by default for relative times and date labels) is a Tab stop?
The Team page says the “source” is cut with an ellipsis, but a team has no source part (only the Group has “Synced from directory”). Should “source” be removed from the Team page?

Image gallery’s text is a generic media-family text: “When to use” repeats the overview word for word, “When not to use” says “Keep sources and actions explicit.” (an instruction, not a case to avoid), and Behavior, Accessibility and Content talk about forms, FileRow, Carousel and “Save metadata”, which are not part of a gallery. Should this page get its own written text?

Video’s text is shared word for word with Audio and the other media pages; “When to use” repeats the overview and “When not to use” is “Keep sources and actions explicit.” Should Video get its own text (for example when to use Video versus Audio)?

The Audio page shows the Video text: its overview says “audio and video” and its parts include picture in picture, which audio does not have. Should Audio get its own text without the video-only parts?

The approved DataGrid sample moves "Reference tables in documentation and settings" out of When to use and corrects it to "Static facts, in documentation or settings: use Table" under When not to use. A text replacement cannot move a list item, so I left it. Should it be moved by hand (deleted from When to use, added to When not to use)?

The Table says its header row can be hidden for a name/value table (options.headerVisible false), but the Property table page says every name/value list of reference facts is a Table with a header row. Which is right: may a name/value table hide its header row?
The static Table is announced to screen readers as an interactive grid ("An ARIA grid"). A table with nothing to operate is normally announced as a plain table. Is the grid role intended here?

It says TagInput and the rename field show a focus underline (--plx-sys-shadow-underline-focus). The field focus rule says focus recolors the border only, with no underline. Is this sentence outdated?

The Counter pill is a solid colored pill, while the pill rule says every pill is soft (light fill, border, dark text). Is the Counter an exception to the pill rule? Also, the Warning counter is called "amber" while the Badge calls the same family yellow: should it say yellow?
"A count beside a label: use Count": there is no component named Count; the counting component is Counter. Should it say Counter?
The Card purpose says it "opens" the object, but the Static card variant does not open. Should the purpose say the card usually opens its object (or can open it)?

It says Active is success and Review is info, and that the soft variant suits a column of statuses. The Badge now has an Active variant (blue, for in progress), info is an old name for it, and every pill is soft. Which tone should Active and In review use here, and may the soft-variant remark go?

It says a lozenge is solid for emphasis or soft in lists, but every Badge is now soft (solid is ignored). Its When to use also says "a short state or category", while a category is a Tag, not a Badge. Should both be corrected to: always soft, and a status only?

It says a List can be numbered (<ol>), but the List's parts describe only an unmarked <ul> with icons. Can a List be numbered? It also says rows people act on are "an interactive list or a table"; under the owner's rule that would be a DataGrid. May I change "a table" to "a DataGrid" once the numbering question is settled?

This page says the DataGrid turns into a list under 600px wide, but the shared write-up below (Behavior, responsive) says the grid scrolls sideways inside its frame. Which is right? Also, narrow="table" is named as the static Table’s setting: is that correct, and is it the Table’s or the DataGrid’s option?

Every page in this group repeats the full DataGrid write-up word for word (purpose, anatomy, behavior, accessibility, content). Should these variant pages show only what is special about them and link to the DataGrid page for the rest?

The Editable table and Tree table pages show the DataGrid’s own write-up (purpose, parts, behavior, accessibility, content), word for word. I left it unchanged here so it is rewritten once, on the DataGrid page, using the DataGrid sample you approved. Is that right?

Chart pages call the values view under each chart the “data grid” (Chart foundations, Chart tooltip, Data label, Annotation, Chart interaction, Line chart), but your rule makes it a static Table (Chart foundations itself says “the same values as a Table”). Should these pages say “data table” (or “the table”) instead, so no one reads it as a DataGrid? I left the wording as it is.

The Threshold page shows the Reference line’s purpose and write-up. That purpose speaks of “a target, an average, a limit or a date”, while Threshold’s own “when not to use” sends averages to the Reference line. Should Threshold get its own purpose (a limit the data should stay under or above), or is the shared text fine? I did not change it.
“The presence dot carries a shape from 40px” is unclear. Does it mean the presence dot adds a shape (not only a color) on avatars 40px and larger? I did not change it.

“The value from the scale’s format or format” repeats a word. Does the second “format” mean the line’s own format setting (so: “the scale’s format, or the line’s format setting”)? It is shared with Threshold, so I did not change it.

This page says the keyboard reading of values (one Tab stop, arrow keys through the points) is "the same on every chart". But the bar, combo, pie, bullet, box plot, radar, Sankey and timeline pages say nothing in their plot takes focus and the keyboard only reaches "Show the data". Which is right: should every chart be readable point by point with the keyboard, or only some? I left this page and those pages unchanged until you decide.

Charts call their table of values the "data grid" (here and in the anatomy of almost every chart page). Under your rule, DataGrid is the dynamic table (sort, filter, group, search) and Table is the static one. A chart’s values table looks static, so should these pages call it the "data table" (a Table) instead of the "data grid"? The accessibility page also says "the data grid and its rows keep their own keys", which suggests something interactive. I changed none of these words.

The overview describes the new metric card (header with icon, title, info, period filter and More; 12 types, 5 layouts, 5 appearances; Panel’s frame; the whole card is the link with href). The written sections below describe the older card (a Card surface; only the title is a link and "the rest of the card is not a target"; title, period, value, change, trend). Which one is current? The written sections probably need rewriting from the new design, which is more than a wording change, so I left both unchanged.
The overview says "the appearance" (5), while the approved decision calls them "styles" (5 styles). Which word should the spec use?
"The largest 24px across its radius" is unclear: does the largest bubble have a 24px radius (48px wide), or is it 24px wide? I left the sentence as it is.

The "With outliers" variant says the values beyond the whiskers show "as points of the frame". What does "of the frame" mean here? If it just means points on the plot, I can shorten it to "The values beyond the whiskers, as points."

The step chart’s purpose is the line chart’s general purpose ("lets people compare the trends of a few series"); it says nothing about values that hold and then jump. Should it get its own purpose, for example "Shows values that change at moments and hold in between, such as prices or limits"? I did not change it.

"Subtotals (total without a value) at natural breaks": does "total without a value" mean a data entry marked as a total and given no amount (the chart works the running total out)? If so I can write it that way; for now it stays as it is.
The Spinner overview says it comes "in two sizes", but the page shows three (Small 12px, Medium 16px, Large 24px). Should the overview say three sizes?

The Empty state page tells people to use it for content that could not load (tone="error", with Retry), and it has an Error variant. But its Behavior and Content sections say "an error is not an empty state" and "do not use it for errors". Which is right? There is also a separate Error state page that covers the same case.

The Empty state overview only describes an application with nothing in it yet, shown in the main region. The page also covers the small version inside a list or panel, and the no-results case. Should the overview describe the component in general?
Skeleton says not to use it for waits "under a second"; the Shimmer page says "under half a second". Which limit is right?

The Success toast says to show nothing for a save that always works, but the Snackbar page gives "Saved" as its main example, and the toast’s own writing guidance uses "Saved" as an example. Should a plain save show a toast or not?
The Snackbar overview says a toast "leaves on its own", but a danger toast stays until it is dismissed. Should the overview mention that exception?

Presence indicator and Availability indicator describe the same thing. Presence indicator shows the Status dot write-up, which says the dot is always 6px, uses the feedback colors, and gives examples like "active, paused, priority". The page itself says presence uses its own colors (never the feedback ones) and larger dots with shapes. Should Presence indicator show the Availability indicator write-up instead, or be merged with it?

Your status display rule says statuses are shown as a status badge with an icon, never a dot. Health indicator, Severity indicator and Status dot all show a status as a dot with words. Do these pages still stand, or should they point to the status badge?
Severity indicator names three levels (info, warning, danger) but says not to use "more levels than the four tones". Is the fourth level neutral, or should it say three?
The Notification page names a component "NotificationList", but the notification center is built from ActivityList. Which name is right?
The Status badge overview says the badge has an icon when color must not carry the meaning alone, but the Badge parts list has no icon. Does the badge carry an icon?

The purpose says a banner offers “the one action” that resolves it, but the parts list and the “Banner with actions” page allow one or two actions. Should the purpose say “one or two actions”, or should banners have only one action?

“The owner removes the banner when it is pressed”: “owner” here seems to mean the code that shows the banner, not a person. Can it read “pressing it removes the banner” (the app’s code does the removing)?
The “With message” page says to use a message on every overlay, but the parts list calls the message optional. Is the message required on every overlay, or optional?

“The spinner turns (still with reduced motion)” can be read two ways: that it keeps turning with reduced motion, or that it stands still. The Accessibility section says that with reduced motion the veil appears at once and the spinner stands still. Can Behavior say that plainly: “The veil fades in and the spinner turns; with reduced motion, neither moves”?

“The toast slides in and out (still with reduced motion)” can be read as “it still slides with reduced motion”. The Accessibility section says that with reduced motion the toast appears at once. Can Behavior say: “The toast slides in and out; with reduced motion it appears at once”?

The page says a confirmation dialog is for destructive or irreversible actions, and that actions which can be undone should use a toast with Undo instead. But the "Confirm" variant says it is for "an action that can be undone or that others will see". Which is right: is the plain Confirm variant meant for undoable actions that others will see (publish, send, share), or only for irreversible ones?
The Destructive variant mentions "larger actions". Does this mean larger buttons than the Confirm variant? If so, which size? The rest of the page says the dialog is always the small size.

The overview says the drawer "slides from a side" and the "Drawer at the end" page says it "slides in from the end edge", but the Motion row says "it does not slide". Should the wording say "docked to a side" (no animation), or does the drawer now slide in?

The "Drawer at the end" page says navigation drawers come from the start edge, the "Drawer at the start" page says top-level navigation is never a drawer, and the Scrim page lists "a navigation drawer over a narrow window" as a use of the light scrim. Is a navigation drawer allowed (for example on narrow windows), or never?

This page says that on Medium and Wide windows the same Sheet is a full-height side sheet. The Sheet write-up says that on Wide windows it becomes a dialog (unless a pane is shown). Which is right for Wide windows?

This page says the inspector (SidePanel) opens as a drawer over the main region on narrow windows. The Bottom sheet page says that at Narrow the inspector opens as a bottom sheet. Which does the inspector become on a phone-width window: a drawer or a bottom sheet?

Below 1024px the open panel lies over the page with a scrim, but it does not take or trap focus (a non-modal layer). The Scrim page says a scrim belongs behind modal layers only. Should the overlaid panel be modal (take and trap focus), or should it have no scrim?

The title guidance says "Keep it to one line; long names wrap in the title." Should long titles wrap onto more lines, or stay on one line (cut off with an ellipsis)? The same text is on the Properties panel page.

The panel footer puts the primary action first ("Save", "Cancel"), while dialogs put Cancel before the primary action. Is the different order on purpose? The same text is on the Properties panel page.

The overview calls the menu surface "a raised panel ... with the menu radius and elevation", but the Contrast row says it has "no shadow drawn (border only)". Is the menu raised with a shadow, or flat with a border only?
The menu write-up says it "does not flip to fit the viewport", but the Floating positioning page says every anchored overlay, menus included, flips and shifts to stay in view. Which is current?

Show more / less shows the Collapsible section write-up, whose purpose is about "a section of content under an accent uppercase title". Show more is a button under a list or a long text, with no such title. Should this page get its own purpose (and write-up), for example from ShowMore or Text? The Expand / collapse page has a similar mismatch (it also covers Panel and NavList group buttons).

Truncate / expand shows the Text write-up, whose purpose is about the type scale ("a style from one short scale ... one key figure, an opening paragraph"). Should this page get a purpose about cutting long text and showing more, or is the Text purpose intended here?

The Scrim says it "fades in with the layer above it (the fast duration)", but Dialog says it "appears and leaves without a transition" and has nothing to reduce. Does the dialog backdrop fade in or not?

The Hover card page shows the Popover’s keyboard and focus write-up (Enter or Space opens it, Escape sends focus back to the trigger), but the Hover card’s own overview says keyboard focus opens it at once and Escape closes it without moving focus. Which is right for the hover card? Should the hover card get its own behavior write-up?
Popup, Inline dialog and Hover card show the Popover’s full write-up word for word. Is that intended (they are the Popover), or should each page link to the Popover page instead of repeating it?
The overview says the rich tooltip has no arrow, but the placement variants on this page (Bottom, Top, Start) describe an arrow pointing at the trigger. Does the rich tooltip have an arrow or not?

The four placement variants (Tooltip below, above, at the start, at the end) and the overview’s last sentence describe the plain tooltip, not the rich tooltip. Should these placements move to the Tooltip page, or do they apply to the rich tooltip too?
The anatomy lists the spotlight as part of the bubble, while the overview calls the Spotlight a separate component the bubble uses. Should the spotlight stay in the bubble’s anatomy?

The three size variants (Medium, Large, Full screen) all say the same thing (“uses the same controls and persistence contract”) and share generic use and avoid lines that say nothing about when to pick each size. What should each size be for?
The anatomy’s third part is “guarded close.” (lower case, with a period), and the anatomy names no step indicator or Back and Next buttons. What are the parts of a wizard dialog?

The wizard dialog’s behavior, accessibility and content text is generic (it mentions “Save copy, Resume draft, Archive and Restore” and status badges) and the content “guidance” row repeats the When-to-use lines. Should this page get a write-up of its own before it is reworded?

The help panel’s write-up talks about things that are not in a help panel: matrix checkboxes, permission summaries, tours, teaching bubbles and the actions “Share” and “Save permissions”. It looks copied from other pages. Should the help panel get its own write-up?

The three variants (In the inspector, Search, Articles) share the same text, and their use and avoid lines (“Use this composition when it fits the task”, “Keep education optional and permissions explicit”) do not describe them. What does each variant show, and when should it be used?
The overview repeats the purpose word for word. Should the overview describe the panel’s parts (a heading, a search field, results, an article with Back) instead?

The variant pages say their messages sit “on the left” and mine “on the right”, but the write-up says mine sit on the end side and flip in right-to-left languages. Should the variant pages say “start side” and “end side” instead of left and right?

The Asset grid page shows the purpose and full write-up of the Asset browser template (“Shows how a data-management capability is put together…”), not of the grid itself. Should this page show the content grid’s own purpose and write-up?

Should they be written for this page, or left for the later pass that hides empty rows? I did not change them.
The "guidance" row repeats the page’s purpose word for word. Should it be removed, or should it say something else?
"Unsaved-changes check — closing asks before losing work" is the only anatomy entry without (required) or (optional). Which is it?
"VisuallyHidden adds words a screen reader needs that the layout shows" reads backwards — should it be words the layout does *not* show?
The `label` part has no "(required)" or "(optional)" marker, unlike the other parts; which is it?

The overview defines contained tabs as "folder tabs joined to a bordered panel", while use[0] names "Folder tabs" as a separate choice for when the whole page body switches. Are contained tabs a kind of folder tab, or are Contained and Folder two different variants (and which name should the overview use)?
It lists "brown (drawn in orange)" among the data hues; is brown still a data hue name, or should it read orange (the Brown category was retired in the color consolidation)?

Both describe chat message bubbles (someone else's message on the start side; the person's own in the action color), not a typing indicator. Are these variant pages on the wrong item, or should the text describe the indicator?
The sentinel is called "a very thin strip" yet "one window tall"; which is right (thin strip, or a strip one window tall)?
The string ends "The row menu on a row's button or right-click:" followed only by tokens; the row menu's items seem to be missing. What does the row menu contain?

"Initialize first; arguments are checked." is too terse to simplify safely — does it mean a call before initialization is refused with an error, and invalid arguments are rejected? Which wording is right?

The text describes loading PDF.js, cancelling outdated renders and exposing text/keyboard scrolling/errors — none of it is pointer behavior. Should it move to loading/a11y, and what is the pointer behavior?

fields: Choropleth map, Donut chart, Pie chart, Gauge, Sankey diagram, Treemap, Word cloud (content[1])
text: These pages carry the shared chart line "Label axes with the measure and its unit, and avoid acronyms.", but none of these charts has axes. Should each drop the line, or get its own rule (a choropleth labels its color scale legend; a donut or pie labels slices with the part name and share; a gauge labels the value with its unit and range; a Sankey labels nodes with totals; a treemap labels tiles; a word cloud explains size in a legend)?
The Gantt axis is time, not a measure. Should it read "Label the time scale with its unit (days, weeks or months)"?
Radar spokes are axes that share one scale. Keep the shared line, or say "Label spokes with the measure name"?
The shared title line ("the question the chart answers") may not fit a single-value meter. Keep it, or replace it with a gauge rule?

The shared chart rule asks for a title written as a question or finding, but a sparkline is word-sized, sits next to the number it describes and has no title. Drop or replace this line for sparklines?
"Label axes with the measure and its unit" contradicts behavior[1] "Do not show axes, grid lines or legends." Which is right?
"none names a distinct object list, and SAP Fiori is the main system that defines one" reads as a contradiction. Does "none" mean none of the compared systems, with SAP Fiori outside that set?
use[1] names the qualifiers "Current" or "Draft"; anatomy[1] and content[1] say "Latest". Which qualifier is right?
"Do not end the label with an ellipsis-only message." Does it ban a label that is only "…", or ending labels with an ellipsis?
"Filled — tinted background with a bottom line" conflicts with the Plenix field rule (a filled field has a border; no underline). Which is right?

"Change only the border color on focus and error" conflicts with the Plenix invalid state (2px danger border plus the lightest red fill). Should focus recolor the border only, with error following the invalid rule?
"Provide data grids or summaries for charts": does "data grids" mean the DataGrid component, or a static Table as the chart's text alternative?
The anatomy lists "serial comma use" as a Plenix rule, but commonGround says systems differ and no string says whether Plenix uses the serial comma. Does it?
"Do not treat disabled controls as a reason to pass off unreadable active content." Does it mean active content never borrows the disabled-control contrast exemption?
"Not applicable; content rules follow the overlay rendered inside." reads as placeholder text. Keep it, or drop it and keep only content[1]?
"Not applicable beyond the overlay's own text." reads as placeholder text. Keep it, or replace it with a content rule?

"At the bottom on compact screens; as a rail on wider ones" overlaps Bottom navigation, whose avoid[1] says not to use it on wide screens. Are these one item, or should the rail case be named differently?
The overview calls the parts links, but behavior says "Disable or hide the control" at the start and end; links cannot be disabled. Should the end state be "hide" only?
It says "permanently removing an object" but also "with recovery when possible", and use[1] prefers undo when the item can be restored. Is deletion permanent, or should "permanently" go?

Anatomy lists a "link" variant (seven values) while the Overview says six variants and "never looks like a link". Is `link` retired (drop it from Anatomy), or should the Overview mention it? Left unchanged.

"arrow keys move between them, Tab leaves" contradicts docs.behavior.focus ("Every control keeps its own Tab stop (there is no roving tabindex)") and keyboard ("Tab and Shift+Tab move through the controls as usual"). Which is right? rec.purpose ("instead of many Tab stops") depends on the same answer; both left unchanged.

"Every control keeps its own Tab stop ..., except that unchecked options of a radio group inside it are skipped by the arrow keys": is the exception about Tab stops or only about arrow keys? Left unchanged.

Says the formatting toolbar has "one Tab stop", but the parent Toolbar docs say every control keeps its own Tab stop (no roving tabindex). It also lists undo/redo among toggle (pressed) buttons. Which is right? Left unchanged.
Says "the groups themselves do not wrap", while Toolbar says "The row and each group wrap onto more lines". Is DataToolbar an intended exception? Left unchanged.

Gives "the views of a list" as an example, but a view switch is a choice of one value, which its own avoid sends to SegmentedControl (Action panel uses a Segmented view switch). Change the example? Left unchanged.
Purpose is Button's ("Lets people cause an action ... one primary per area ..."), wrong for a dialog trigger. Write a specific purpose (actions-modal-trigger has one)? Left unchanged.
Purpose is Button's, wrong for a drawer trigger. Write a specific one? Left unchanged.
Purpose is Button's, wrong for a popover trigger. Write a specific one? Left unchanged.
Purpose is Button's, wrong for a disclosure trigger. Write a specific one? Left unchanged.
Modal trigger and Dialog trigger describe the same thing (a button that opens a dialog, focus returns to it, ellipsis when more input is needed). Merge or differentiate them? Left unchanged.

The purpose says the bar sits "under the command bar, always shown" and "the command bar itself never changes on selection", but rec.text deprecates BulkActions for CommandBar's selection state and use[0]/avoid[0] (owner, 2026-10-15) say that under a command bar its selection swaps the bar. Left unchanged: should the purpose describe the bar as the selection bar of a page with no command bar?

The text and purpose present BulkActions as "the selection bar under the command bar", which contradicts the deprecation and the owner rule (2026-10-15) that under a command bar its selection swaps the bar. Left unchanged: should this page point to CommandBar's selection state instead?

The purpose is the selection bar's (BulkActions), which is wrong for an overflow action. Left unchanged: which purpose should it carry (e.g. "Keeps every action reachable when a row is too narrow, by moving the last ones into More")?

The purpose is the whole action menu's ("Keeps a set of actions behind one button so the surface stays calm, and opens them as a list people can choose from with pointer or keyboard."), not a menu item's. Left unchanged: give it its own purpose?
Carries the action menu purpose, which does not describe an on/off option. Left unchanged: give it its own purpose?
"use a group of choices": does this mean the radio menu item (MenuRadioGroup)? If so it could name it; left unchanged.
Carries the action menu purpose, which does not describe a group. Left unchanged: give it its own purpose?

The Small variant’s use, “A secondary floating action beside a list”, implies a second floating action on a screen, but the page says “More than one per screen” is avoided and content.actions says “One per screen”. Which holds? Left unchanged.

“format and size when the file is large or comes in several formats” versus avoid “Several formats or sizes: a menu of downloads”: is a file in several formats one button with its facts, or a menu? Left unchanged.
rec.text says the name gives “the file and its format”; a11y.name also includes the size (“cross-014.png (PNG, 4.2 MB)”). Should the overview add the size? Kept as written.

“Sentinel — an invisible hairline as tall as the reveal distance, where the button is drawn”: a hairline cannot be tall, and “where the button is drawn” is unclear (where it is placed, or what it observes?). Left unchanged until the intended meaning is confirmed.
The Focus row in Accessibility holds a target-size rule (“at least the standard control height”), not a focus rule. Move it to another row? Left unchanged.
"Opening moves focus into the field" repeats docs.behavior.focus. Drop it here (keep only the result count), or keep it because it tells what a screen reader hears on opening?
The rule says "no slash", but the error example is "A name can’t contain / or \". Is the backslash also refused? If so the rule text should say "no slash or backslash".

"Nothing is disabled" sits under Focus and overlaps docs.behavior.error. Does it mean the Duplicate button is never disabled? If yes, may it read "Duplicate is never disabled: …" (and move out of Focus)?

The overview and the purpose are the same imperative sentence ("Choose a supported source before importing records."), and it says nothing about what Import brings in. Should the overview become a description (e.g. "Imports records from a source people choose first: a file, pasted text or a URL") and the purpose a reason (e.g. the guide’s "add content in bulk instead of creating it by hand")? Left unchanged.

File, Paste and URL share one text that says nothing about each source, and the same text stands in docs.behavior.pointer although it is not pointer behavior. Write a text per source and real pointer behavior? Left unchanged.

"Use this composition when it fits the task." and "Keep scope and consequences explicit before submitting." are filler on every variant (the second is not a when-not-to-use). Write real ones, or remove? Left unchanged.

text: These are shared text from a family (Import, Export, Request access, Upgrade, Delete account): "wizard step", "review grids and shortcut groups", "permission summaries", "Badge roles", "keyboard bindings", "Request access, Upgrade and Delete account", "plan terms and account names" do not apply to Import. Keep them as shared rules (moved later), or trim each page to what applies? Left unchanged.
The purpose repeats the overview word for word. Should it say why (e.g. the guide’s "take data out of the app for use in other tools")? Left unchanged; the overview was rewritten.

Same as Import: Format, Selection or all records, and Background export share one text, the same filler use/avoid, and the same text stands in docs.behavior.pointer. Write per-variant text? Left unchanged.
Usage says people can choose fields, but the anatomy has no field chooser (format, scope, background option, Badge/Link). Is choosing fields supported?

text: Same shared-family text as Import ("wizard step", "review grids and shortcut groups", "permission summaries", "Request access, Upgrade and Delete account", "source columns, plan terms and account names"). Keep or trim? Left unchanged.
